title: Spectral assembly of the affine Jacobian log-determinant inequality
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (2026-08-09), proof of Theorem 1.4.5 on PDF pp. 45-46: entropy along the displacement map uses the Jacobian (1-t)I+t∇T and convexity of -log det; https://chewisinho.github.io/main.pdf#page=46
target_statement: For a finite real Hermitian matrix A, identify det((1-t)I+tA) with the product of the affine eigenvalues. For positive-definite A and 0≤t≤1, use the existing eigenvalue-level log inequality to derive the literal matrix inequality t log det(A) ≤ log det((1-t)I+tA), together with the equivalent -log det orientation.

searched: Pinned Mathlib v4.33.0: Mathlib/Analysis/Matrix/Spectrum.lean (spectral_theorem and det_eq_prod_eigenvalues)

shared_floor_audit.notes: Mathlib supplies Hermitian diagonalization and determinant-as-product-of-eigenvalues, while Samplinglib already supplies conjugation invariance and the diagonal affine determinant/log inequalities. No existing theorem assembles these into the literal affine Jacobian determinant used by Chewi. No currently evidenced Riemannian/Optimisation consumer requires this exact log-determinant statement, so it remains route-local rather than prematurely becoming a shared API. The implementation is a new isolated sibling module and does not edit the active transport/Brenier stabilization files.
